Music tablet in her paws whenever Spotify is open
Say each new song in a bubble
Curl up and sleep when I'm away
Tails (a zenko earns a new tail with wisdom)
Inari bib (the red shrine bib under her bell)
Retro typewriter font in the fox's speech bubbles

Nag me even without a session
Start a break when a session finishes
Whisper accuracy (bigger = more accurate, slower; downloads once)
Whisper isn't installed for the Python I can see, so Windows' built-in speech is used (less accurate). Press Install Whisper.
Talk out loud and she answers out loud. Your voice is turned into text on this PC by whisper.cpp (free, offline). Nothing is sent anywhere.
Not set up yet. Set up downloads about 62 MB once (GitHub + Hugging Face).
More accurate (181 MB, a bit slower)

If the school network blocks the download: at home, get whisper-bin-x64.zip from github.com/ggml-org/whisper.cpp/releases and ggml-base.en-q5_1.bin from huggingface.co/ggerganov/whisper.cpp, unzip both into one folder, then 'Use files I downloaded'.

The anime voice needs the free VOICEVOX app running (Customize > Her voice). She says the Japanese version of her answer out loud while the chat stays in English (switch that off in Customize > Her voice). The English voice is picked in 'Fox's voice' below.
Get pages ready in the background (instant page switching)
Motion level lives in Customize > Look and feel. On battery, Auto calms the animations.

High-resolution pixel art (same designs, smoother edges, many more pixels)
Shrine-style titles (Zen Old Mincho for page and card titles)

The app font is Zen Maru Gothic: soft and round, made in Japan, and easy to read. Pick another one under Look > Font. Both fonts are free (SIL Open Font License) and come inside Zenko, so nothing gets installed on your PC.
Roaming (she walks about, naps on windows)
never during focus sessions or lock-in
Match the real weather in my home city
Day and night (yawns, nudges me to bed)
minutes of screen time (a 5-min break resets them)
Ask how I'm feeling once a day (mood journal)
Track (original music made on your PC)
Shrine garden  (soft koto, a low hum and a glass wind chime)
Bamboo rain  (a breathy bamboo flute over gentle rain)
Moon temple  (slow temple bowls and a deep, calm drone)
Allow internet lookups (weather, news, web search)
Search the web when Zenko doesn't know something
Home city (used when you just say 'weather')

When you're online, a free online AI finds the answer (Gemini can also search the web), then your own models on this PC re-check it so it uses IB DP terms and the 2027 syllabus. Offline, or if the free limit runs out, Zenko just uses your PC's models like before.
Your free key (saved only on this PC)

Gemini key in 1 minute: 1) press 'Get a free key' and sign in with a Google account. 2) Press 'Create API key'. 3) Copy it, paste it above, press Test. No card needed. Free limits are small but plenty for studying.
Privacy: with this on, your tutor questions, files you ask about and screenshots you send to chat go to the online AI. Zenko never sends your screen on its own.
Open this window when the app starts

One-time setup (uses your Premium account):
1. Open the Spotify dashboard, log in, Create app (any name).
2. Redirect URI: paste the one below. Tick 'Web API'. Save.
3. Copy the app's Client ID here, then press Connect.
Play music when a focus session starts (pause on breaks)
Focus playlist (name of one of yours, or a search like 'lofi beats')
Music presets  (say 'play focus', 'play my favourite song'...)
Type a name to search, or paste a Spotify link (in Spotify: Share > Copy link).
Battery meter on the fox's tail (warns when low)
Dates in files are day-first (05/12 = 5 December)
Drifting snow, petals or fireflies in the sidebar
Tell her exactly what to close and what to leave open in focus sessions and lock-in. Your rules come first, top to bottom. Example: YouTube + “bio, cell, khan” → Keep open.
Text size (it also grows and shrinks with the window)
Shrine frame around the window (reopen the window to see it change)
Make flashcards from my Study book chats automatically
Pop quiz from my due cards now and then when I'm not in a session
Show the exam countdown on her ema plaque
Nudge me about IA / EE / TOK deadlines
Let YouTube videos about my subjects through in focus sessions and lock-in
Extra words that mean a video is for study (comma separated, e.g. a teacher's or channel's name)
First exam day (YYYY-MM-DD), for the countdown

Where updates come from: a GitHub name like yourname/zenko (free GitHub Releases), or a link to a latest.json file on your website.
If the school network blocks the download, get the new zenko.py at home (or from the website) and use 'Install from a file'.
Sky follows the time of day (soft dawn, day and dusk; night stays the shrine)
Seasons and weather in the sidebar and garden
Foxfire wisp when you switch pages
Dim foxfire progress glow in the window frame during focus
The little fox at the top acts out the page you're on
Fox poses now and then (stretches, play bows, naps, pounces)
Study alerts and reminders are said in
Link with Zenko Browser (share my calendar with its new tab)
Let her notice what I'm reading there
Both apps only read each other's small files in %APPDATA%\FoxBuddy. Nothing goes online.
Join the Town square when I'm online
Message server (ntfy). Leave as it is unless you run your own:
Find study time for homework-like emas

An ema like “finish bio IA by friday” or “revise chem” gets sessions in your free half hours (from the Upcoming clock) before it's due, around your exam plan. Emas at a set time keep that time free. Say “plan my emas”, “bio IA takes 3 hours” or “don't plan call mum”.

The moment a distracting site or app comes to the front, she pounces on it, eats it, and sends you back to work. Exit any time: say 'unlock', right-click her > Exit lock-in, or hold Esc for 2 seconds.
What she does with a distraction
Smart: close just that browser tab, hide other apps
Close it (tab or the whole app)
Start a focus session with it
Extra things that count in lock-in (one per line: a word in the window title, or an app like discord.exe). Your normal distracting sites always count too.
Auto-plan study before exams (on my timetable)
Most sessions per subject in one day
Mark my free hours on the clock
